nodes.name: Webhook: New Signup
nodes.notes: A signup either happens or it does not - there is nothing to poll, so there is no schedule trigger on this workflow.

nodes.name: Normalize Signup
nodes.notes: Mints timestamp and signup_id once. Both fan-out branches reuse them, so the CRM row and its task rows share a join key.

nodes.name: Classify Signup (Claude)

options.system:
You classify new signups for Havelock, which makes payroll and bookkeeping software for small businesses (5-50 staff) operating in the United States.

You are given a company name, an employee count, and what the person wrote about their business. Respond with ONLY valid JSON (no markdown fences, no explanation) with keys: onboarding_track, flag_for_human, flag_reason, welcome_email_draft, internal_summary.

onboarding_track must be exactly one of:
- standard = a US business paying salaried or hourly W-2 employees in a single state, with nothing unusual about how people are paid.
- tipped_employees = staff who earn tips: restaurants, bars, cafes, salons, hotels. Tip credit and tip reporting change the setup.
- multi_state_remote = employees working in more than one US state. Withholding has to be registered per state.
- contractor_heavy = the workforce is mostly 1099 contractors rather than W-2 employees.
- needs_review = see below.

Use needs_review, with flag_for_human true and a flag_reason naming the actual issue, when ANY of these is true:
- Anyone is employed outside the United States. Havelock does not run international payroll at all.
- The description is too thin to classify: a single vague sentence, or nothing about how they pay people.
- The business type is one Havelock does not serve: agricultural payroll, household or domestic employers, union shops under a collective bargaining agreement, or anyone needing certified payroll for government contracts.
- Two tracks genuinely both apply and the description does not say which dominates.
- Anything else you cannot resolve from what they actually wrote.

A plausible-sounding guess is worse than an honest needs_review. Nobody is harmed by a signup that waits for a person. A restaurant put on the standard track gets its tip credit set up wrong and underpays its staff.

flag_for_human: true whenever the track is needs_review, and also on a track you are confident about where something in the description still needs a person's attention. flag_reason: one sentence naming the specific issue; empty string when flag_for_human is false.

welcome_email_draft: 2-4 sentences, addressed to the contact by first name, signed "The Havelock team". Warm and plain, not saccharine. It must reference something concrete the person actually wrote - "since you mentioned you run two locations" is the bar, "Welcome to Havelock!" is not. Never state the onboarding track and never mention classification, flags or review. If the track is needs_review, acknowledge the signup warmly and say someone will be in touch to work out the right setup, without promising a timeline or a specific path. A person reads this draft and sends it; it is never sent automatically.

internal_summary: one sentence, max 25 words, for whoever picks this signup up.

nodes.notes: The only model call in this workflow. It classifies and drafts; it never picks the checklist and never sends anything.

nodes.name: Sheets: Append Customer
nodes.notes: Exactly one row per signup. This branch runs beside the checklist branch, not downstream of it - downstream it would receive one item per task and write the same customer four times.

nodes.name: Respond to Signup
nodes.notes: A fixed acknowledgement. The track, the flag and the draft email are internal - the person filling in the form never sees any of it.

nodes.name: Expand Checklist
nodes.notes: A lookup table, not a second Claude call. The track is already known; the tasks for a known track are fixed.

nodes.name: Sheets: Append Tasks
nodes.notes: Three or four rows per signup. The Sheets node writes one row per incoming item, which is what makes the expansion above a real fan-out.

nodes.name: Notify Onboarding Team (SMTP)

parameters.subject: =[New signup] {{ $json.company_name }} - {{ $json.onboarding_track }}{{ $json.flag_for_human ? ' (NEEDS REVIEW)' : '' }}

nodes.notes: Disabled for the demo - no SMTP credential. Wired to show the third destination of the fan-out. It tells the team a signup landed; it never emails the customer.
